name: DG Interns Hub Weeks 2 to 5
description: Techniques seen in Weeks 2 to 5. Blue = Week 2, green = Week 3, orange = Week 4, purple = Week 5.

techniques.comment: Week 2. Failed logons I generated on my Windows laptop. Log source: Windows Security log, Event ID 4625.

Week 2, Week 3 and Week 5. A dummy local user was created (net user). Log source: Security Event ID 4720 (Weeks 2 and 5) and Sysmon Event ID 1 (Weeks 3 and 5). In Week 5 I repeated it as a test and no alert fired.
Week 2 and Week 4. Successful logon, and the valid SSH password found after the brute force. Log source: Security Event ID 4624, Ubuntu auth.log in Splunk.
Week 2. A new Windows service was installed. Log source: System log, Event ID 7045.
Week 2. The Security log was cleared after a backup copy was saved. Log source: Security Event ID 1102.
Week 3 and Week 5. PowerShell was run on my laptop. Log source: Sysmon Event ID 1 (process create). In Week 5 I ran an encoded PowerShell test, Splunk showed 1 event and no alert fired.
Week 3 and Week 4. Nmap SYN scan. Detection: my Snort rule 1000004 Nmap SYN Scan Detected, alert forwarded into Splunk in Week 4.

Week 5. A dummy scheduled task was created with schtasks on my laptop as a test and deleted after. Log source: Sysmon Event ID 1 (schtasks.exe), Splunk showed 1 event. Security Event ID 4698 was not logged because Windows auditing was off, and no alert fired.
Week 4. Hydra SSH password guessing from Kali against the Ubuntu VM. Log source: Ubuntu auth.log in Splunk (failed logins counted by source IP).
Week 5. All 3 phishing samples used links to lookalike or unrelated domains. Evidence: email headers, urlscan.io, VirusTotal, AlienVault OTX.
Week 5. Seen in 2 public Any.Run reports, not in my own lab. The user had to open a malicious file. Source: Any.Run process tree.
Week 5. Seen in a public Any.Run report, not in my own lab. wscript.exe ran a JavaScript file from a zip. Source: Any.Run behaviour list.
Week 5. Seen in a public Any.Run report, not in my own lab. The script decoded a Base64 file. Source: Any.Run behaviour list.
Week 5. Seen in a public Any.Run report, not in my own lab. The script and PixelLite83.exe read system information. Source: Any.Run.
Week 5. Seen in a public Any.Run report, not in my own lab. The script checked if a folder exists. Source: Any.Run.
Week 5. Seen in a public Any.Run report, not in my own lab. The script saved data to a binary file. Source: Any.Run.
Week 5. Seen in a public Any.Run report, not in my own lab. DNS query to a duckdns.org domain. Source: Any.Run Network Threats, Suricata rule.
Week 5. Seen in a public Any.Run report, not in my own lab. A file was created in the Startup folder and launched from a Registry key. Source: Any.Run.
Week 5. Seen in a public Any.Run report, not in my own lab. UAC bypass by modifying the registry. Source: Any.Run.
